topics.label: The full lifecycle of POST /todos with a due date and email
topics.question: Walk me through exactly what happens, in order, when a client sends POST /todos with a due date and an email.
topics.answer_hint: Pydantic validation, the dependencies resolve (sync get_db in the threadpool plus the key check), insert, commit and refresh (refresh loads created_at), add_task with primitive values, 201 response, then the task runs after the response. See app/routers/todos.py:27-40.

topics.label: How API keys isolate each tenant's todos
topics.question: How does a user only ever see their own todos?
topics.answer_hint: The validated key is returned as the tenant id; list filters on owner_key == key (app/routers/todos.py:21); patch and delete go through _get_owned, which returns 404 for someone else's todo. See app/deps.py:18-21.

topics.label: Why a sync SQLAlchemy Session inside async def handlers blocks the event loop
topics.question: Your handlers are async def but use a sync SQLAlchemy Session. What does that do to the event loop, and would plain def have been better?
topics.answer_hint: Blocking database calls on the loop thread serialise every request; def handlers run in the threadpool; real async needs AsyncSession with an async driver (asyncpg/aiosqlite). See app/routers/todos.py:14-24.

topics.label: Backing up the '60% lower p95 via async' claim
topics.question: Your CV says moving database access to async cut p95 by 60%. Where is that in this code, and how did you measure p95 before and after?
topics.answer_hint: There's no async engine or driver in requirements.txt and no benchmark (app/database.py:6-7). You need a concrete load-test story (tool, concurrency, before and after numbers) or a reworded bullet.

topics.label: Whether Taskly actually runs on PostgreSQL
topics.question: I set DATABASE_URL to a Postgres URL and start the container. Does it work?
topics.answer_hint: No psycopg driver installed, a SQLite-only check_same_thread connect argument (app/database.py:6), and create_all instead of migrations (app/main.py:15).

topics.label: When reminders actually fire and what a restart does to them
topics.question: When does the reminder email actually go out, and what happens to queued reminders if the container restarts?
topics.answer_hint: It runs right after the response, not at due_at; BackgroundTasks live in process memory, so a restart drops them, with no retry; the send is a stub (app/services/notifications.py:12-13). See app/routers/todos.py:38-39.

topics.label: PATCH with an explicit null and NOT NULL columns
topics.question: I send PATCH /todos/1 with {"title": null}. What happens?
topics.answer_hint: The schema accepts None, exclude_unset keeps explicit nulls, and the NOT NULL column (app/models.py:14) raises IntegrityError, so the client gets a 500. See app/schemas.py:13.

topics.label: How the tests get a clean database (StaticPool, overrides, env at import)
topics.question: How do your tests get a clean database, and why StaticPool and the env var at the top of the file?
topics.answer_hint: Each in-memory SQLite connection is a fresh database, so StaticPool shares one connection; dependency_overrides swaps get_db; config reads env at import time, so API_KEYS is set first. See tests/test_todos.py:3-28.

topics.label: The end-to-end path of one video through Clipper
topics.question: Walk me through what happens to one video, from being found in the folder to clips on disk.
topics.answer_hint: ffprobe duration, then one full decode for scene detection, then grouping in Python, then up to max_clips ffmpeg cuts run one after another. See clipper.py:58.

topics.label: Getting scene-change timestamps out of ffmpeg
topics.question: How do you get scene-change timestamps out of ffmpeg?
topics.answer_hint: select='gt(scene,T)' keeps frames above the threshold, showinfo logs them to stderr, and a regex pulls out pts_time. The quotes protect the comma, and there's no -loglevel because showinfo logs at info. See clipper.py:26.

topics.label: How pick_highlights chooses which moments win
topics.question: How does pick_highlights decide which moments win?
topics.answer_hint: Greedy windows tied to each group's first cut, ranked by number of cuts, top N kept, 1 s lead-in, put back in time order, dropped if they run past the end. See clipper.py:35.

topics.label: Stream copy vs re-encode: keyframes and accurate cuts
topics.question: Why is stream copy the default, and what exactly does --reencode buy you?
topics.answer_hint: Copying costs almost nothing but starts on the previous keyframe; re-encoding decodes up to the seek point, so the cut is frame-accurate, at the cost of running libx264. See clipper.py:48.

topics.label: ThreadPoolExecutor vs processes, and CPU oversubscription
topics.question: Why a ThreadPoolExecutor rather than processes or asyncio, and how did you choose 4 workers?
topics.answer_hint: The threads only wait on child processes, so the GIL doesn't matter; but each ffmpeg is multi-threaded itself, so workers × ffmpeg threads oversubscribes the cores. See clipper.py:81.

topics.label: What a corrupt file or missing ffmpeg does to a batch
topics.question: A file is corrupt and the detection ffmpeg exits non-zero. What does the user see? And what if ffmpeg isn't on PATH?
topics.answer_hint: detect_scenes has no check=True, so it returns [] and the video is logged as '0 clips' (clipper.py:26). Only CalledProcessError is caught (clipper.py:87), so a FileNotFoundError or ValueError breaks the logging loop and crashes the run.

topics.label: Backing up the 'hardware-accelerated encoding, 3x faster' claim
topics.question: Your CV says hardware-accelerated encoding cut processing time by 3x. Show me where, and where would hardware actually help this pipeline?
topics.answer_hint: There's only software libx264 behind an opt-in flag (clipper.py:51), and the default path doesn't encode at all; the main cost is the full-resolution decode in detect_scenes, so hardware decoding or downscaling is where speed would come from.

topics.label: Turning Clipper into a 500+ videos/day service
topics.question: Turn this into something that reliably processes 500+ videos a day. What would you build?
topics.answer_hint: About 173 s per video on a single serial worker; a job queue (Celery/Redis), S3 in and out, idempotent output keys, timeouts and retries, non-zero exit codes and metrics, a container with a pinned ffmpeg version, and tests. See clipper.py:80.
